correctness.rationale: A first-write state must have all four labels in its upper interval. For n≤2 fewer than four states have an interval of size at least four. For n=3 exactly 000 and the three unit vectors qualify, so they must bear distinct labels. Each unit-vector interval has four states and is rainbow. The top vertex lies in all three and must take the label of 000; a weight-two vertex lies in two such intervals and must take the label of the remaining unit vector. Conversely these antipodal fibers give rainbow intervals; from 000 take the four light states as outputs both when starting and when the first write left it at 000, so a single state-dependent update function works. The parity map has kernel {000,111}, and labeling the four distinct fibers gives 4! maps. The proof is exhaustive on the exact Boolean cube.
residual_risks: No claim about generation-dependent decoding or uniqueness of update rules. The optional packaged census was inspected as code, not independently run.

originality.rationale: The minimum three-cell construction, its decoder formula and codeword pairs are prior. The supported distinct claim is the converse that every generation-independent extendable decoder has precisely those four fibers, with 24 labeled maps. The inspected foundational papers and exact catalogues do not establish that converse; the assessed novelty is search-bounded.
residual_risks: Earlier exhaustive searches or equality-case observations in non-indexed notes may exist. No assertion of global priority or of originality of the known construction or rate is made.

value.rationale: It completes the equality case of the foundational optimal four-message WOM block, distinguishing forced decoding geometry from flexible encoder choices. The repetition-code cosets are a necessary structure, not just a convenient canonical choice, a useful fact when this small block is used in constructions. It is the rigidity, not the elementary multiplication by 4!, that carries value.
residual_risks: This is a complete equality classification of one motivated optimal block, not a general uniqueness or capacity theorem.
